newsitem.title: USA: NY panel approves NYNEX/AT&T interconnect pact.
newsitem.headline: NY panel approves NYNEX/AT&T interconnect pact.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said on Tuesday it approved an interconnection agreement between NYNEX Corp and AT&T Corp that will ease AT&T's entry into the local telephone market.

The commission said in a news release that the three-year agreement details the terms and conditions under which AT&T can compete with NYNEX by providing local service through NYNEX's own network. In a separate news release, NYNEX hailed the agreement as a significant step toward allowing NYNEX in turn to compete for long-distance customers.
"NYNEX is ready, willing and able to compete with AT&T," the local phone company said in its release.

The commission said this is the first such agreement NYNEX has finalized with one of the three biggest long-distance companies. Last month NYNEX said it agreed to a draft interconnection pact with MCI Communications Corp.
AT&T already has reached 15 similar interconnection deals with local Baby Bell service companies in other states.
NYNEX plans to merge with Bell Atlantic Corp.
